# NvTrace Data Model Validator

## Introduction

`DataModelValidator` collects a live trace from the NVIDIA Nsight Perf service, builds the offline data model, and checks trace completeness using GoogleTest. It can also export the captured data as a Perfetto trace.

## Usage

```shell
./DataModelValidator \
    --duration-ms 10000 \
    --processN 1 \
    --output validation.perfetto-trace
```

Run the CUDA workload in another terminal during the collection window. Choose a duration long enough to cover the workload. Open the optional exported trace in [Perfetto](https://ui.perfetto.dev).

The service must collect CUDA Driver API tracing, GPU kernel events, CPU/GPU clock calibration, and GPU performance counters for the corresponding checks. The counter-sample check assumes 1000 Hz sampling. See the [service configuration documentation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nsight-perf-daemon/blob/main/README.md).

For a workload with a known number of immediate kernel launches, add `--launches <count>`. Enable CUDA Runtime API tracing in the service and add `--enable-cudart-trace` to also check Runtime API launch counts.

The test uses a temporary Trace Stream Database and removes it when the test finishes.

## Options

- `--duration-ms <ms>`: collection duration; default `2000`.
- `--processN <count>`: expected number of processes in the data model; default `1`.
- `--launches <count>`: expected immediate kernel launch count; default `0xFFFFFFFF`, which skips launch-count comparisons.
- `--enable-cudart-trace`: also check CUDA Runtime API launch counts when `--launches` is set; default `false`. This option does not enable tracing in the service.
- `--output <path>`: export a Perfetto trace with debug events; default is no export.

GoogleTest options are also supported. Place `--gtest_*` options before the validator options.

## Validation

The test checks CPU clock calibration and the expected process count. For each captured GPU partition, it checks GPU clock calibration and the number of GPU performance-counter samples. When `--launches` is set, it also compares API launch counts and resolved immediate kernel launches with the expected count. CUDA Graph launches are not included in these comparisons.

Count comparisons allow a tolerance: 5% plus 300 events for API calls, 10% plus 300 for resolved kernel launches, and 15% plus 300 for counter samples. The expected counter sample count equals the collection duration in milliseconds, assuming 1000 Hz sampling.

GoogleTest reports assertion failures, and the executable returns a nonzero status if validation fails. Check workload timing, the expected process and launch counts, and the service configuration when investigating a failure. Unrelated captured processes can cause the process-count check to fail.

# NvTrace CUDA Continuous Profiling Test

## Introduction

This sample profiles seven CUDA workloads: vector addition, CUDA Graphs, multi-GPU execution, coupled BF16 HMMA, tensor-core matrix multiplication, immediate memset operations, and host callbacks. Run it as a smoke test after building the SDK.


## CUDA Toolkit Reference

The Coupled BF16 HMMA sample is original to the NVIDIA Nsight Perf SDK. The other illustrated samples can be found in the [CUDA Samples repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-samples).

## How to Open the Trace Files

1. Build the SDK package.

2. Launch `./TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling` application
```shell
./TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling
```

3. Open the generated `nvtrace.perfetto-trace` in <https://ui.perfetto.dev>.

## How to Run the Sample

There are 7 samples from which you can **select** which ones you would like to run using the argument `--samples`. You can also select the **number of iterations** in each sample by using the argument `--iterations`.

| Number Selection | Samples      |
| -----------------| ------------ |
| 0 (default)      | All Samples  |
| 1                | VectorAdd    |
| 2                | CUDA Graphs  |
| 3                | MultiGPU     |
| 4                | Coupled BF16 HMMA |
| 5                | Tensor Cores |
| 6                | Immediate Memset |
| 7                | Host Callbacks |

**Examples**

Run only MultiGPU and Coupled BF16 HMMA:

```shell
./TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling --samples 3,4
```

Run all seven workloads 20 times each:

```shell
./TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling --iterations 20
```


Run MultiGPU and Coupled BF16 HMMA 20 times each:
```shell
./TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling --samples 3,4 --iterations 20
```

## Options

- `--iterations <count>`: iterations per selected workload; default `5`.
- `--timeout-ms <ms>`: maximum wait for service initialization.
- `--samples <ids>`: comma-separated workload selections; default `0` for all.
- `--nvtrace <bool>`: enable or disable NvTrace profiling; default `true`.
- `--snapshot <bool>`: use `TsfSnapshotConsumer` instead of `StreamingConsumer`; default `false`.
- `--trace-output-path <path>`: exported Perfetto trace path; default `nvtrace.perfetto-trace`.
- `--help`: print usage.

# NvTrace CUDA Samples

This directory contains CUDA examples, tests, and benchmarks for the NVIDIA Nsight Perf SDK:

- [`benchmarks`](benchmarks/README.md) measures profiling overhead.
- [`tests/DataModelValidator`](tests/DataModelValidator/README.md) validates captured trace data.
- [`tests/NvTraceContinuousProfiling`](tests/NvTraceContinuousProfiling/README.md) demonstrates continuous profiling of CUDA workloads.
- [`cuda-samples`](cuda-samples/README.md) contains selected NVIDIA CUDA Samples sources used by the examples.

## Compatibility

The sample source and test behavior themselves have the lowest stability level and may change between SDK releases. They are not compatibility interfaces.

## Contributions

Contributions require signed-off commits and the Developer Certificate of Origin. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a change.

## Security

Do not report potential security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues. Follow the private reporting process in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## License

NVIDIA-authored SDK source is licensed under Apache-2.0; see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Imported/adapted files under `cuda-samples/` retain their BSD-style terms in [cuda-samples/LICENSE](cuda-samples/LICENSE). See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for dependency licenses and attribution.

# CUDA Samples

This directory contains selected source files imported or adapted from [NVIDIA CUDA Samples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-samples) for use in the NVTrace CUDA profiling tests.

## Compatibility

Compatibility with the complete upstream CUDA Samples repository is not guaranteed.

## License

The imported files retain their original NVIDIA copyright notices and license terms. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and the notices in each file.

The Apache 2.0 license used elsewhere in this repository does not apply to these imported files.

## Contents

- `include/` contains the CUDA Samples helper headers.
- `src/` contains the vector addition, integer Tensor Core GEMM, CUDA graphs, and multi-GPU workloads.

Some files have been adapted for integration with the NVTrace tests, including changes to entry points, tracing, and test assertions. This directory contains a selected subset of CUDA Samples, rather than a complete import.

# NvTrace CUDA Benchmarks

## Introduction

The benchmarks evaluate the performance impact of NvTrace profiling, focusing on both system-level and end-to-end overhead. Included artifacts are:

* **BenchmarkNvTraceCuda**: End-to-end CUDA benchmarks that test various kernel launch patterns and CUDA API calls
* **BenchmarkNvTraceMemory**: Memory operation benchmarks that measure `cudaMemset` and `cudaMemcpy` (H2D, D2H, D2D, H2H) throughput across multiple buffer sizes
* **BenchmarkNvTraceServiceInitialization**: Measures NVIDIA Nsight Perf service start/stop latency (forks a new service each iteration)
* **RunCudaBenchmarks.sh**: Automated script that ensures consistent benchmarking conditions (e.g., environment setup, warm-up runs, repeatability)

## Usage

### Building

The benchmarks are built as part of the NVIDIA Nsight Perf SDK samples.

### Running Benchmarks

To achieve consistent and reliable results, use the provided script which sets the CPU to a fixed frequency:

```bash
# Run end-to-end CUDA benchmarks without NvTrace (baseline)
sudo ./RunCudaBenchmarks.sh base

# Run end-to-end CUDA benchmarks with NvTrace enabled (service + target hooks)
sudo ./RunCudaBenchmarks.sh nvtrace

# Run end-to-end CUDA benchmarks under Nsight Systems
sudo ./RunCudaBenchmarks.sh nsys

# Run service initialization benchmark (noisy; forks each iteration)
sudo ./RunCudaBenchmarks.sh nvTraceServiceInit
```

**Note**: sudo privileges are required for the script to set the CPU clock to a fixed frequency

## Benchmark Categories

### CUDA Benchmarks

* **CPU-limited scenarios**: When the GPU kernel is small and CPU cycles are fully occupied, profiling overhead becomes measurable. This is often observed in applications that launch many tiny kernels back-to-back.
* **GPU-limited scenarios**: When the GPU kernel is large and the CPU is mostly waiting for GPU execution, profiling overhead is typically lower.

| Benchmark Name | Description | Workload Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EndToEnd** | Complete vector addition workflow (memory allocation, kernel launch) | Vector Operations | I/O Bandwidth limited scenarios |
| **KernelAdd** | Vector addition kernel execution only | Vector Operations | CPU limited scenarios |
| **KernelLargeWorkload** | Complex vector operations with tanh function | Vector Operations | GPU limited scenarios |
| **SyncKernel_Empty** | Synchronous empty kernel launches | Immediate Kernel Launch | CPU limited scenarios |
| **SyncKernel_WaitforNsec** | Synchronous kernels with specified wait times (1μs, 10μs, 100μs) | Immediate Kernel Launch | from CPU-limited to GPU-limited |
| **AsyncDenseKernel_Empty** | Asynchronous empty kernel launches | Immediate Kernel Launch | CPU limited scenarios |
| **AsyncDenseKernel_WaitforNsec** | Asynchronous kernels with specified wait times (1μs, 10μs, 100μs) | Immediate Kernel Launch | from CPU-limited to GPU-limited |
| **AsyncSparseKernel_Empty** | Sparse asynchronous kernel launches | Immediate Kernel Launch | CPU limited scenarios |
| **AsyncSparseKernel_WaitforNsec** | Sparse asynchronous kernels with specified wait times (1μs, 10μs, 100μs) | Immediate Kernel Launch | from CPU-limited to GPU-limited |
| **AsyncGraphKernel_Empty** | CUDA Graph-based kernel launches | Graph Kernel Launch | |
| **AsyncGraphKernel_WaitforNsec** | CUDA Graph kernels with specified wait times (1μs, 10μs, 100μs) | Graph Kernel Launch | |
| **cudaDriverGetVersion** | CUDA Runtime API version query | Runtime API | Isolates runtime API trace overhead for a very fast function |
| **cuDriverGetVersion** | CUDA Driver API version query | Driver API | Isolates driver API trace overhead for a very fast function |
| **cuGetDeviceCount** | Device enumeration | Driver API | Isolates driver API trace overhead for a very fast function |
| **cudaStreamTest** | CUDA stream operations | Runtime API | Isolates runtime API trace overhead for a very fast function |
| **SyntheticTest_Async1us1000TimesThenSync** | 1000 asynchronous 1μs kernels followed by synchronization | Synthetic | |

### Memory Benchmarks

`BenchmarkNvTraceMemory` measures raw memory-operation throughput for `cudaMemset` and `cudaMemcpy` across four buffer sizes (1KB, 64KB, 1MB, 16MB). Run with `--nvtrace=false` for baseline bandwidth or `--nvtrace=true` to measure NvTrace overhead on memory operations.

**Direct API benchmarks** call `cudaMemset` / `cudaMemcpy` (or `cuMemcpy` for H2H) synchronously on each iteration.

**Graph benchmarks** record a single memset or memcpy node via CUDA stream capture (`cudaStreamBeginCapture` / `cudaStreamEndCapture`), instantiate the graph once, then time repeated `cudaGraphLaunch` calls.

**Converted graph benchmarks** build explicit `CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_MEMSET` / `CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_MEMCPY` nodes inside a conditional graph body (matching `CudaApiTraceInDriverGraphNodeTest`). During `cuGraphInstantiate`, the driver lowers these memory nodes to internal kernel nodes.

| Benchmark Name | Description | Transfer Direction |
|---|---|---|
| **Memset_Device** | `cudaMemset` on a device buffer | N/A |
| **Memcpy_H2D** | Host-to-device copy | Host → Device |
| **Memcpy_D2H** | Device-to-host copy | Device → Host |
| **Memcpy_D2D** | Device-to-device copy | Device → Device |
| **Memcpy_H2H** | Host-to-host copy via CUDA driver API (`cuMemcpy`) | Host → Host |
| **MemsetGraph_Device** | `cudaMemsetAsync` captured into a graph, launched via `cudaGraphLaunch` | N/A |
| **MemcpyGraph_H2D** | H2D `cudaMemcpyAsync` graph node | Host → Device |
| **MemcpyGraph_D2H** | D2H `cudaMemcpyAsync` graph node | Device → Host |
| **MemcpyGraph_D2D** | D2D `cudaMemcpyAsync` graph node | Device → Device |
| **MemcpyGraph_H2H** | H2H `cuMemcpyAsync` graph node (pinned buffers) | Host → Host |
| **MemsetGraphConverted_Device** | Memset node lowered to kernel during graph instantiation | N/A |
| **MemcpyGraphConverted_H2D** | H2D memcpy node lowered to kernel during graph instantiation | Host → Device |
| **MemcpyGraphConverted_D2H** | D2H memcpy node lowered to kernel during graph instantiation | Device → Host |
| **MemcpyGraphConverted_D2D** | D2D memcpy node lowered to kernel during graph instantiation | Device → Device |

```bash
# Run memory benchmarks without NvTrace (baseline bandwidth)
./BenchmarkNvTraceMemory --nvtrace=false

# Run memory benchmarks with NvTrace enabled
./BenchmarkNvTraceMemory --nvtrace=true
```

### Service initialization benchmark

| Benchmark Name | Binary | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **BM_NvTraceServiceInitialization** | `BenchmarkNvTraceServiceInitialization` | Service creation and destruction time per iteration |

import os
import time
import select
import signal
import subprocess
import sys

# Start nvidia-nsight-perf and verify it starts correctly
def start_service_host(service_host_command):
    try:
        # Start nvidia-nsight-perf
        service_host_process = subprocess.Popen(service_host_command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)

        expected_messages = ["Initializing", "Creating", "Service created"]
        for expected_message in expected_messages:
            ready, _, _ = select.select([service_host_process.stdout, service_host_process.stderr], [], [], 5)
            if ready:
                line = service_host_process.stdout.readline()
                if not line:
                    line = service_host_process.stderr.readline()
                    if not line:
                        print("nvidia-nsight-perf terminated unexpectedly")
                    else:
                        print(line.strip(), flush=True)
                    sys.exit(1)
                print(line.strip(), flush=True)
                if expected_message not in line:
                    sys.exit(1)
            else:
                print(f"Timeout waiting for nvidia-nsight-perf to initialize")
                sys.exit(1)
        return service_host_process
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error starting nvidia-nsight-perf: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

# Start NvTrace streaming consumer (observer)
def start_nvtrace_streaming_consumer(nvtrace_streaming_consumer_command):
    try:
        # Start the NvTrace streaming consumer
        nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process = subprocess.Popen(nvtrace_streaming_consumer_command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)

        expected_messages = ["Initializing", "Creating database", "Starting", "Press enter"]
        for expected_message in expected_messages:
            ready, _, _ = select.select([nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.stdout, nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.stderr], [], [], 5)
            if ready:
                line = nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.stdout.readline()
                if not line:
                    line = nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.stderr.readline()
                    if not line:
                        print("NvTrace streaming consumer terminated unexpectedly")
                    else:
                        print(line.strip(), flush=True)
                    return None
                print(line.strip(), flush=True)
                if expected_message not in line:
                    return None
            else:
                print(f"Timeout waiting for NvTrace streaming consumer to initialize")
                return None
        return nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error starting NvTrace streaming consumer: {e}")
        return None
                        

# Run the workload to be profiled
def run_workload(workload_command):
    try:
        # Run the workload process and wait for it to complete
        subprocess.run(workload_command, check=True)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running workload: {e}")

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print(f"Usage: python {os.path.basename(__file__)} <workload> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]")
        return

    # nvidia-nsight-perf should be in the same directory as this script
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    service_host_command = [os.path.join(script_dir, "nvidia-nsight-perf")]

    # Workload command from the remaining command line arguments
    workload_cmd = sys.argv[1:]

    # Start nvidia-nsight-perf
    service_host_process = start_service_host(service_host_command)
    if not service_host_process:
        return

    # Start the observer process
    nvtrace_streaming_consumer_command = [os.path.join(script_dir, "nvtrace_streaming_consumer"), "--stop-on-enter-key"]
    nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process = start_nvtrace_streaming_consumer(nvtrace_streaming_consumer_command)

    if nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process:
        # Run the workload process
        run_workload(workload_cmd)
        print("Workload completed; stopping NvTrace streaming consumer")
        # Send enter to the streaming consumer
        nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.stdin.write('\n')
        nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.stdin.flush()
        nvtrace_streaming_consumer_process.wait()

    # Send Ctrl-C to the nvidia-nsight-perf process
    service_host_process.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)
    service_host_process.wait()
    print("nvidia-nsight-perf terminated")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

NVIDIA is dedicated to the security and trust of our software products and services, including all source code repositories managed through our organization.

If you need to report a security issue, please use the appropriate contact points outlined below. **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through GitHub.** If a potential security issue is inadvertently reported via a public issue or pull request, NVIDIA maintainers may limit public discussion and redirect the reporter to the appropriate private disclosure channels.

## Reporting Potential Security Vulnerability in an NVIDIA Product

To report a potential security vulnerability in any NVIDIA product:
- Web: [Security Vulnerability Submission Form](https://www.nvidia.com/object/submit-security-vulnerability.html)
- E-Mail: psirt@nvidia.com
    - We encourage you to use the following PGP key for secure email communication: [NVIDIA public PGP Key for communication](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/pgp-key)
    - Please include the following information:
        - Product/Driver name and version/branch that contains the vulnerability
        - Type of vulnerability (code execution, denial of service, buffer overflow, etc.)
        - Instructions to reproduce the vulnerability
        - Proof-of-concept or exploit code
        - Potential impact of the vulnerability, including how an attacker could exploit the vulnerability

While NVIDIA currently does not have a bug bounty program, we do offer acknowledgement when an externally reported security issue is addressed under our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy. Please visit our [Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/psirt-policies/) policies page for more information.

For all security-related concerns, please visit NVIDIA's Product Security portal at https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security

# NVTX Trace needs nvtx3's CUDA driver injection discovery.
get_target_property(nvtx3IncludeDirectories nvtx3 INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES)
if(NOT nvtx3IncludeDirectories)
    get_target_property(nvtx3LinkLibraries nvtx3 INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES)
    foreach(nvtx3LinkLibrary IN LISTS nvtx3LinkLibraries)
        if(TARGET ${nvtx3LinkLibrary})
            get_target_property(nvtx3LinkLibraryIncludeDirectories ${nvtx3LinkLibrary} INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES)
            if(nvtx3LinkLibraryIncludeDirectories)
                set(nvtx3IncludeDirectories ${nvtx3LinkLibraryIncludeDirectories})
                break()
            endif()
        endif()
    endforeach()
endif()
if(NOT nvtx3IncludeDirectories)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Could not resolve the nvtx3 include directories from the nvtx3 target")
endif()
set(CudaSamplesSourceDir
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../cuda-samples"
)

add_library(CudaSamples OBJECT
    src/hmmaCoupledFlops.cu
    src/ImmediateMemset.cu
    src/HostCallbacks.cpp
    ${CudaSamplesSourceDir}/src/immaTensorCoreGemm.cu
    ${CudaSamplesSourceDir}/src/simpleCudaGraphs.cu
    ${CudaSamplesSourceDir}/src/simpleMultiGPU.cu
    ${CudaSamplesSourceDir}/src/VectorAdd.cu
)

target_include_directories(CudaSamples
    PRIVATE
        ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include
        ${CudaSamplesSourceDir}/include
)
# nvcc keeps its bundled CUDA Toolkit nvtx3 ahead of target_include_directories, so pass nvtx3's include on the CUDA command line instead.
target_compile_options(CudaSamples BEFORE PRIVATE
    "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-I${nvtx3IncludeDirectories}>"
)

target_link_libraries(CudaSamples
    PRIVATE
        NvTraceTestUtilities
        # Keep nvtx3 ahead of the CUDA Toolkit's NVTX. Include precedence follows link order, and
        # this target's NVTX events may not be traced if the CUDA Toolkit's NVTX wins.
        nvtx3
        CUDA::cuda_driver
        CUDA::toolkit
        googletest
        nvtrace_client
)

add_executable(TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling
    src/NvTraceServiceTests.cpp
    src/CudaContinuousProfiling.cpp
)

target_include_directories(TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling
    PRIVATE
        ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include
)
target_include_directories(TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling BEFORE PRIVATE
    ${nvtx3IncludeDirectories}
)

target_link_libraries(TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling
    PRIVATE
        NvTraceTestUtilities
        # Keep nvtx3 ahead of the CUDA Toolkit's NVTX. Include precedence follows link order, and
        # this target's NVTX events may not be traced if the CUDA Toolkit's NVTX wins.
        nvtx3
        CUDA::cuda_driver
        CUDA::toolkit
        CudaSamples
        cxxopts
        googletest
        nvtrace_client_offline
)
nvtrace_link_cuda_runtime(TestNvTraceCudaContinuousProfiling)
